blocks.title: What Your AI Receptionist {{Agent Runs}}
blocks.description: The whole intake-to-rebook lifecycle of a cleaning business, handled in conversation.

cards.title: Answers Every Inbound Call
cards.description: Picks up on the first ring at any hour - including the stacked mornings when every crew is already on site and nobody can reach the phone.

cards.title: Texts Back Missed Calls
cards.description: Any call that still slips through gets a text within seconds, while the prospect is on your listing rather than the next company's.

cards.title: Scopes the Job in Conversation
cards.description: Beds, baths, square footage, pets, add-ons, and access details captured from plain speech instead of a form the customer abandons.

cards.title: Quotes From Your Rate Card
cards.description: Applies your flat rates, service-area rules, and minimums, and flags the jobs that genuinely need a walk-through before a number goes out.

cards.title: Books the Crew on Your Calendar
cards.description: Holds a real slot against crew availability and writes the job into the scheduling tool your office already works from.

cards.title: Confirms, Reminds, Reschedules
cards.description: Sends confirmations, arrival windows, and reminders, and moves an appointment when the customer asks - without a call to the office.

cards.title: Triages After-Hours and Urgent Work
cards.description: Handles evening, weekend, and holiday inquiries, and escalates genuine emergencies by the rules you set.

cards.title: Chases Quotes That Went Quiet
cards.description: Follows up on unconverted estimates on your schedule instead of letting them age out in a spreadsheet.

cards.title: Sells the Recurring Plan
cards.description: Offers weekly, biweekly, or monthly service at the moment the one-time clean is booked - the point where the customer is most likely to say yes - and handles renewals later.

cards.title: Follows Up After the Visit
cards.description: Checks that the clean met expectations, asks for the review when it did, and routes the conversation to a human when it did not.

rows.leftTitle: The phone rings while everyone is on a job
rows.leftDescription: Crews cannot stop mid-clean and the office is one person deep, so the busiest hours are exactly when calls go to voicemail.
rows.rightTitle: Every call answered on the first ring
rows.rightDescription: Coverage does not depend on who is free. Volume spikes, evenings, and weekends are handled the same way.

rows.leftTitle: The fastest reply wins, and yours comes hours later
rows.leftDescription: Homeowners contact three or four companies in one sitting. By the time someone calls back, the job is usually already booked elsewhere.
rows.rightTitle: First response in seconds, on their channel
rows.rightDescription: The agent replies where the inquiry arrived, immediately, and moves straight into scoping and booking.

rows.leftTitle: Quotes go out and nobody chases them
rows.leftDescription: Estimates sit unanswered because follow-up is manual and the next day's schedule always takes priority.
rows.rightTitle: Every quote followed up until it resolves

rows.leftDescription: Calls, web forms, WhatsApp photos, and marketplace inquiries live in different places, so context is lost and customers repeat themselves.
rows.rightTitle: One agent on every channel, one history
rows.rightDescription: A marketplace lead who follows up by text keeps the whole conversation - no repeated questions, no lost details.

rows.leftTitle: Recurring plans get sold only when someone remembers
rows.leftDescription: Recurring work carries the margin, but the offer depends on whoever is on the phone thinking to make it.
rows.rightTitle: The recurring offer is made every time
rows.rightDescription: Every eligible one-time booking gets the weekly, biweekly, or monthly option at the right moment in the conversation.

items.question: How is this different from the answering service we already pay for?
items.answer: An answering service takes a message and hands it back to your office, so the actual work - scoping, pricing, and booking - still waits for a human. This agent finishes the job in the same conversation: it scopes the clean, applies your rates, holds a real slot on your calendar, and writes the job into your scheduling tool.

items.question: What does the agent handle on its own, and when does a person step in?
items.answer: It handles standard intake end to end: qualifying, quoting from your rate card, booking, confirming, reminding, rescheduling, and following up. You decide what it never decides alone - non-standard pricing, complaints, damage claims, commercial contracts - and it hands those over with the full conversation attached.

items.question: Does it work for our service mix - one-time deep cleans, recurring maid plans, commercial janitorial?
items.answer: Yes, and it treats them differently. One-time jobs are scoped and priced on the spot, with the recurring plan offered at the moment of booking. Recurring customers are recognised, so the agent handles schedule changes and renewals instead of re-qualifying them. Commercial and specialty work follows its own rules, including routing to a walk-through.

items.question: What about commercial accounts that need a walk-through before a price?
items.answer: The agent is told which requests cannot be priced over the phone. For those it collects the details that make the visit productive - site size, frequency, scope, access, decision maker - then books the walk-through on the right person's calendar rather than guessing at a number.

items.question: Who owns the customer data and the call recordings?
items.answer: You do. Conversations, recordings, and records stay in your account and are never used to train public AI models. You set retention windows, and you can export or delete the data at any time.

items.question: How long does deployment usually take?
items.answer: Most cleaning operators are live in about 5 to 15 days. What moves that number is how ready your inputs are: a clear rate card and service-area rules, access to your scheduler and CRM, and the escalation rules you want. Starting from a template and letting the AI Concierge draft the canvas removes most of the setup time.

items.question: What should we expect to change in speed-to-lead and missed calls?
items.answer: First response moves from hours to seconds, and the calls that used to reach voicemail during stacked job days get answered or texted back immediately. The published benchmarks behind those effects, and the caveat that results vary by service mix and coverage, are set out in the section above.

items.question: How do credits map to call and message volume?
items.answer: Credits are consumed by what the agent actually runs - conversation turns, channel usage, and the actions it takes in your systems - so a quiet week costs less than a busy one. There is no monthly fee and no per-seat charge, and credits do not expire. The pricing page carries the current per-channel rates and credit packages.

items.question: Can we extend the platform beyond lead handling once we are running?
items.answer: Yes. The same canvas runs recruiting intake for cleaners, dispatch and crew communication, collections reminders, and reporting workflows. Most operators start with inbound booking because it pays for itself first, then reuse the connections and templates for the next process.
